summary: Read-only review complete: three security findings and one matrix inconsistency. No edits, builds, tests, network, or .env reads. Referenced ops/db-roles/brand-role.sh is absent from this checkout.

findings.title: Registration claim omits the ceremony-kind boundary
findings.detail: Branch B lists owner/session/nonce/fingerprint checks but omits kind='register'. Branch A's manage/options issues a challenge with those same bindings before any credential proof. Following B literally, a stolen customer session can obtain that challenge, use it for a fresh WebAuthn registration, and submit register/verify without earning a grant. The schema permits identical register/manage shapes. Existing capability redemption explicitly binds kind: packages/api/src/routes/customer-tokens.ts:123-135.
findings.fix: Specify an atomic registration-only claim with hash, kind='register', RP, tenant, owner, session, nonce, fingerprint, expiry and unconsumed predicates. Require a real-route negative control that submits a registration response constructed from a manage/options challenge.

findings.title: Rollback TOTP invalidation leaves reusable step-up authority
findings.detail: The trigger deletes credentials and challenges but preserves step_up_at. The previous image's disable path preserves sessions, and enable explicitly retains the calling session (packages/api/src/auth/admin-staff.ts:104-111). Within the five-minute window, a copied calling-session token therefore retains step-up authority across disable/re-enable. After re-upgrade, its holder can start a new registration bound to the new fingerprint without proving the replacement factor. Registration checks only timestamp freshness; session.step_up_at has no recovery-state binding (packages/api/src/db/schema-core.ts:180-197).
findings.fix: Durably invalidate session authorization during TOTP recovery, including the retained calling session. Clear step-up authority and prevent stale in-flight proofs from restoring it, or revoke the affected sessions. Extend rollback rehearsal to attempt fresh registration using the retained pre-recovery token.

findings.title: Leaving password change unchanged permits recovery overwrite
findings.detail: The explicit decision not to restructure signed-in password change contradicts sections 7 and 11 and preserves a recovery race. packages/api/src/routes/account.ts:382-393 reads the session/password, performs hashing, then updates the customer without rechecking either. With the default non-renewing policy, reset can commit during hashing and revoke that session (packages/api/src/routes/customer-tokens.ts:131-145), after which the stale request overwrites the recovered password and performs the newly required passkey wipes. Fingerprints then recognize the attacker's replacement password as current.
findings.fix: Retain restructuring for password change: verify outside the mutation transaction, lock the customer, revalidate the non-renewing session and verified password-hash snapshot, then update credentials and invalidate dependent authorization atomically. Test reset committing between initial proof and mutation.

findings.title: Passkey-list matrix cannot use the credentials deny-group contract
findings.detail: The design assigns admin management routes HUMAN outcomes with group='credentials', including GET /v1/admin/passkeys. However, packages/api/src/auth/agent-policy.ts:86-90 bypasses GET, so this route reaches requireHuman and returns 'agents cannot perform this action' (packages/api/src/routes/admin-helpers.ts:61-62). The grouped matrix contract instead requires AGENT_NOT_ALLOWED and the credentials boundary message (packages/api/src/sdk/authorization-matrix.identity-cases.testkit.ts:84-99). Its audit expectations also describe a middleware denial that never occurred.
findings.fix: Give GET /v1/admin/passkeys a separate HUMAN contract proving the direct requireHuman denial and unchanged credential state. Keep the credentials deny-group contract on the five authenticated mutations.
